name: Tiles & Stone
tagline: Every floor and wet wall in the project starts here
description: Tiles carry more of an Indian project's area than any other finish, and the difference between a ceramic and a full-body vitrified tile is the difference between a five-year floor and a twenty-year one. Natural stone follows, specified by origin, finish and the maintenance the client is willing to accept.

materials.name: Ceramic tile
materials.blurb: Budget wall and light-traffic floor tile
materials.description: Clay-bodied and glazed, with the pattern only on the surface. Perfectly good on walls and in low-traffic rooms; chip it and the pale body shows immediately, so keep it off busy floors.

materials.name: Vitrified tile
materials.blurb: Low-porosity tile for everyday residential floors
materials.description: Fired to a dense, glass-like body that absorbs almost no water, which is why it dominates Indian residential flooring. Strong, cheap per square foot and available in every finish from matte to mirror-polished.

materials.name: Porcelain tile
materials.blurb: Densest tile body — commercial-grade durability
materials.description: Fired hotter and denser than standard vitrified, with very high abrasion resistance. The right call for shops, offices, lobbies and any home with dogs and a lot of grit.

materials.name: Full-body vitrified tile
materials.blurb: Colour runs right through — a chip does not show white
materials.description: The pigment goes through the entire body, so wear and chipping never expose a different colour underneath. The specification for heavy commercial traffic and any floor expected to last decades.

materials.name: Double-charge tile
materials.blurb: Two layers of pigment pressed 3–4 mm deep
materials.description: A thick double layer of colour makes the pattern survive years of polishing and traffic. The commercial-lobby default in India, though the pattern range is limited to what two feeds can produce.

materials.name: GVT (glazed vitrified tile)
materials.blurb: Digitally printed glaze — photographic marble and wood looks
materials.description: A digital glaze over a vitrified body allows any image: convincing marble, timber planks, concrete. The design freedom is total; the wear layer is only as deep as the glaze.

materials.name: PGVT (polished glazed vitrified tile)
materials.blurb: Mirror-polished GVT that reads like a marble slab
materials.description: GVT taken through a polishing line for a high-gloss, slab-like finish. Stunning in a formal living room and lethal in a wet bathroom — never specify it where feet arrive wet.

materials.name: Subway tile
materials.blurb: Classic 75×150 / 100×200 rectangle for backsplashes
materials.description: The most forgiving wall tile there is — small format, easy to set out around switches, and a grout colour changes the whole look. A perennial in kitchens and bathrooms.

materials.name: Mosaic tile
materials.blurb: Small tiles on mesh sheets — curves, niches and detail work
materials.description: Glass, stone or ceramic chips pre-mounted on mesh, so a curved wall or shower niche can be tiled cleanly. Labour and grout cost more than the tile itself; budget accordingly.

materials.name: Terracotta tile
materials.blurb: Unglazed fired clay — warm, handmade, needs sealing
materials.description: Natural clay tiles with colour variation and a soft, earthy warmth that machine tiles cannot fake. Porous, so they must be sealed and resealed — a maintenance conversation before it becomes a complaint.

materials.name: Outdoor tile
materials.blurb: Thick, textured tile rated for rain, sun and thermal movement
materials.description: Frost- and UV-stable bodies with a rough face for grip. Also available in 20 mm pavers that can be dry-laid on gravel or pedestals for a terrace.

materials.name: Anti-skid tile
materials.blurb: Textured face rated R10–R12 for wet floors
materials.description: The specification that stops a bathroom becoming a liability. Anything that gets wet underfoot — bathroom floors, utility areas, pool surrounds — should be R10 or better.

materials.name: Indian marble
materials.blurb: Makrana, Ambaji and Rajnagar — home-grown and affordable
materials.description: Quarried domestically, so cost and lead time are a fraction of imported stone. Softer and more porous than granite: seal it, keep acids off it, and expect it to develop a patina.

materials.name: Italian marble
materials.blurb: Statuario, Carrara, Botticino — the reference stones
materials.description: Imported marble with the veining that has defined luxury interiors for centuries. Expensive, soft, stain-prone and worth it in the right room — usually one feature area rather than a whole floor.

materials.name: Granite
materials.blurb: Hard, stain-resistant stone for counters and heavy floors
materials.description: Far harder than marble and much more forgiving of Indian kitchen use — turmeric, oil and heat included. Black galaxy, Steel grey and Kashmir white remain the volume choices.

materials.name: Quartzite
materials.blurb: Natural stone with marble looks and granite hardness
materials.description: A metamorphic stone that gives the veining clients want from marble with far better durability. Genuine quartzite is often mislabelled in the market — verify before you specify.

materials.name: Sandstone
materials.blurb: Warm, matte, non-slip stone for courtyards and façades
materials.description: Jodhpur, Dholpur and Kota family stones that weather beautifully outdoors and stay cool underfoot. Naturally textured, so slip resistance comes free.

materials.name: Kota stone
materials.blurb: The dependable Indian utility floor — cheap and tough
materials.description: Blue-green limestone from Rajasthan that has floored Indian service areas for generations. Inexpensive, hard-wearing and increasingly used honed as a deliberate design choice.

materials.name: Slate
materials.blurb: Riven, layered stone with strong natural texture
materials.description: Splits into naturally textured sheets in charcoal, rust and multicolour. Excellent grip outdoors and a strong feature-wall material indoors.

materials.name: Travertine
materials.blurb: Porous cream limestone with a soft, aged character
materials.description: Natural voids give travertine its texture; it can be supplied filled or unfilled. Warm and calm underfoot, but it must be sealed and kept away from acids.
